# Cadence Design Systems (CDNS): research and conditional dated valuation v3

Information cutoff: October 18, 2026. Financial and cash-flow origin: June 30, 2026. USD unless stated otherwise.

## Conclusion

Cadence combines recurring EDA demand with faster-growing IP, hardware and simulation businesses. Demand quality is supported by contractual backlog, but an increasing upfront mix and acquisitive expansion mean that headline growth and non-GAAP profitability overstate neither cash certainty nor free economic earnings by themselves. The operating research and four v2 corrections have passed independent research review. This v3 adds revised compensation economics and conditional common-share allocation, both awaiting independent review. A current-date common-equity valuation remains gated.

After funding future grants separately from legacy-award allocation, the analyst DCF gives June-origin enterprise values of $12.72B downside, $26.00B base and $49.34B upside. Using the explicit default claims and award assumptions below, conditional values are $39.28, $86.51 and $169.51 per common share. These are conditional arithmetic outputs, not verified June values. These are information-through-October reconstructions, not contemporaneous June forecasts, current stock-price targets, or executable trading recommendations. No market price was used to set growth, discount rates or terminal assumptions. No application changes or publication were performed.

## Security and evidence

The issuer is Cadence Design Systems, Inc.; CDNS common stock ($0.01 par value) is registered on Nasdaq Global Select Market. The official [Robinhood security page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/CDNS/) has buy/trade functionality, but this is not account-specific eligibility verification. Its quote text labels a Sunday as a trading session, so no quote or market-cap valuation comparison is used.

The latest filed actuals are the [June 30, 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/813672/000081367226000092/cdns-20260630.htm), filed July 29. The evidence set includes ten annual filings, the latest quarterly filing, prior-year releases, official prepared remarks and CFO commentary, the 2026 proxy, and a privately retained third-party rendering of Q2 Q&A and the September 9 Goldman Sachs interview. Primary prepared remarks take precedence over transcription. Not every page of every historical filing is claimed to have been read; the source ledger specifies financial/footnote scope. The conference event is [officially identified](https://investor.cadence.com/news/news-details/2026/Cadences-Anirudh-Devgan-to-Present-at-Goldman-Sachs-Communacopia--Technology-Conference/default.aspx); the audio was not independently transcribed.

## Business model, visibility and recognition

Cadence has one operating segment. Core EDA, Semiconductor IP and System Design and Analysis are product revenue categories; geographic categories are not operating segments. Q2 revenue mix is 68% Core EDA, 15% IP and 17% SDA. Core EDA includes emulation/prototyping hardware, so treating all 68% as ratable software would be wrong.

Q2 revenue was $1.584451B, 24% above the year-earlier period; H1 was $3.058671B. Q2 Core EDA grew 18%, IP more than 40%, and SDA 37%, according to official remarks. SDA includes Hexagon and cannot be labeled wholly organic. Product category percentages are rounded and do not yield an exact dollar growth attribution.

Only 72% of Q2 revenue was recognized over time. Another 6% was classified as other recurring, making the company’s recurring figure 78%; upfront revenue was 22%. The trailing recurring share was 79%, versus 80% for FY2025 and 83% for FY2024. No audited ARR metric is supplied. Do not multiply a quarter’s recurring revenue by four and label it ARR.

Backlog was $8.1B, including $0.9B of noncancelable commitments for which product selection remains unspecified. Of the remaining $7.2B, 58% is expected in the next 12 months, or $4.176B before rounding to reported $4.2B; 40% is expected in months 13–36. Applying 58% to the full $8.1B would overstate near-term conversion. Potential future royalties are excluded. Invoicing, revenue recognition and cash receipts are different events: deferred revenue was $1.169571B, contract assets $39.824M, unbilled receivables $564.614M, and total net receivables including long-term balances $1.125208B. Hardware/IP acceptance and delivery timing matter.

## What management’s outlook says, and what the model assumes

The [July 27 CFO commentary](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/813672/000081367226000089/cfocommentary07272026ex9902.htm) guides FY2026 revenue $6.26–6.34B, GAAP operating margin 27.75–28.75%, non-GAAP margin 43.75–44.75%, GAAP EPS $4.76–4.86, non-GAAP EPS $8.05–8.15, cash from operations about $2B and capex about $240M. The outlook assumes export controls remain substantially similar. Repurchasing about half of free cash flow is a capital-allocation intention, not additional operating cash generation.

The [official prepared remarks](https://s206.q4cdn.com/597110084/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/CDNS-Q2-2026-Earnings-Conference-Call-Prepared-Remarks.pdf) discuss agent adoption, advanced interfaces, verification hardware and deeper foundry work. Management’s demonstrations and customer engagements are evidence of product activity, not a separately booked AI revenue stream. New workflow agents may create incremental subscription/consumption revenue and increase use of underlying solvers. The model includes no separately invented AI TAM conversion or revenue attributed to engagement counts.

Q2 Q&A emphasized broader software/add-on activity, IP timing, hardware supply constraints and spending for Intel and Hexagon. The September interview described monetization of agents above physics-based engines and argued that more design exploration can absorb efficiency gains. These qualitative statements are management views, not independently measured demand or guaranteed future pricing. The public synthesis is original and bounded; full third-party transcripts remain excluded from the public package.

## Ten-year history and comparability

The attached JSON/CSV cover FY2016–2025 with reported dates, tags, filing accession, source dates and cell provenance. Revenue rose from $1.816B to $5.297B; GAAP operating margin moved from 13.5% to 28.2%. R&D remained substantial, $735M in FY2016 and $1.769B in FY2025. CFO minus capex rose from $391M to $1.587B, but after treating SBC as an economic cost these figures are $282M and $1.132B. These arithmetic cash proxies are not unlevered cash flow and exclude acquisition consideration.

Important breaks:
- FY2016–2017 use ASC605. FY2018 adopts ASC606 using modified retrospective accounting; earlier periods were not restated. A later XBRL revenue tag does not make them ASC606-comparable.
- FY2019 introduces lease capitalization and includes a very large noncash deferred-tax benefit. Its $3.53 EPS is not recurring earnings power.
- FY2020 has 53 weeks. FY2023 onward is calendar-year reporting.
- Product definitions evolved. Earlier verification, digital and custom categories aggregate to Core EDA, and System Interconnect becomes SDA. FY2019 category allocations differ by one percentage point between original tables; the history uses the subsequent FY2020 comparison and flags the conflict.
- Acquisitions broaden revenue. AWR/Integrand, NUMECA/Pointwise, OpenEye/Future Facilities, Rambus interface IP/Pulsic/Intrinsix, BETA CAE and 2025 acquisitions are documented in the separate timeline. Cash paid is not total consideration when stock or service-contingent payments are involved.
- FY2025 includes $128.545M of export-settlement expense; $140.6M of penalties and forfeitures were paid in Q3 2025. The charge is not repeated as a June 2026 debt claim, though ongoing compliance costs/risks remain.

The history is a comparable presentation with known breaks, not a fabricated ten-year organic/recast series. Missing tags remain null rather than zero, with the manually sourced 2025 intangible balance identified explicitly.

## Guidance track record and contradictory source claims

Initial FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 revenue midpoints were approximately $4.03B, $4.58B and $5.18B; actuals were $4.090B, $4.641B and $5.297B, roughly 1.5%, 1.3% and 2.3% above midpoint. Non-GAAP EPS actuals were $5.15, $5.97 and $7.14 versus initial ranges $4.90–5.00, $5.87–5.97 and $6.65–6.75. GAAP margins were not uniformly successful: FY2024’s 29.1% missed 32–33%, and FY2025’s 28.2% missed 30.25–31.25%. Acquisitions, integration, legal items and tax explain why adjusted and GAAP outcomes should both be evaluated.

A specific source inconsistency is preserved: the Q2 CFO commentary says it exceeded revenue guidance, but the prior [Q1 CFO commentary](https://s206.q4cdn.com/597110084/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/Q1-2026-CFO-Commentary-FINAL.pdf) gave $1.555–1.595B. Actual $1.584451B exceeded midpoint but was within the range. Do not repeat a high-end beat.

February 17 FY2026 guidance excluded Hexagon and was $5.9–6.0B revenue and $8.05–8.15 non-GAAP EPS. The acquisition closed February 23; closing expectations added $160M revenue and about $0.28 EPS dilution. April guidance included the acquired operation at $6.125–6.225B and $7.85–7.95 EPS. July raised those to $6.26–6.34B and $8.05–8.15. FY2026 remains guidance, not an observed success. Three completed fiscal comparisons do not establish a ten-year forecasting track record.

## Capital, claims, awards and acquisition funding

The June 30 bridge begins with $1.440443B cash, $2.5B debt principal, $11.165M public equity investments and $80.227M debt securities. Debt carrying value is $2.4822B, after discounts/costs; fair value is about $2.468B. The model uses face debt conservatively. Private/equity-method investments of $89.6M at book are not credited unconditionally. A $189M operating cash reserve is an analyst assumption, leaving $1.251443B excess cash. NQDC trust assets are excluded because they fund employee claims.

Hexagon’s $3.101008B gross consideration included about $2.2B cash and 3.2M issued shares, valued $902.2M, with $154.6M acquired cash. The deal had already closed at the June origin. Opening cash, debt and legal shares reflect it; the model does not deduct the price again. The cash roll-forward reconciles exactly from $3.001317B to $1.440443B using H1 CFO, investing, financing and currency movements. Remaining transaction-tax/retention claims need a separate settlement reconciliation; acquired deferred-tax liabilities are not automatically cash transaction taxes.

Legal shares were 275.393M at June 30. Q2 basic/diluted weighted averages of 273.955M/276.163M are not dated share counts. The [2026 proxy, printed pages 34–35](https://s206.q4cdn.com/597110084/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/CDNS-2026-Proxy.pdf) distinguishes February 19's 1.686228M already-issued restricted shares from 4.475463M unissued RSU/PSU/LTP shares at maximum performance, including 0.338474M vested but unsettled LTP units. Options were 0.994747M, with a $193.12 weighted strike and 3.37-year remaining life. Adding all 6.161691M restricted-stock/unit awards to legal common would count issued restricted stock twice.

The conditional base explicitly assumes February's unissued award and option counts remain unchanged at June. This is not a factual roll-forward. It also assumes 0.30M existing ESPP rights, referenced to January purchases of 0.284404M, not a reported June count. Full participation is allocated to all assumed performance awards, options and ESPP rights. Options/ESPP receive no exercise-proceeds credit, so this is a zero-price full-share allocation convention, not option fair value. It may overallocate that assumed inventory, but does not prove the inventory is complete. The denominator is 275.393 + 4.475463 + 0.994747 + 0.30 = 281.163210M units. Already-issued restricted shares are counted only inside legal common.

Future grants are separately funded. Gross new-grant value proxies from annual restricted-share grants times weighted grant-date fair value, option grants times their fair value, and ESPP purchases times purchase-right value are $413.196M/$546.813M/$468.484M in FY2023/2024/2025, or 10.10%/11.78%/8.84% of revenue. These approximate gross proxies precede forfeitures; ESPP purchases proxy overlapping grant cohorts and accounting award quantities differ from maximum performance units. The revenue-weighted three-year result is 10.18%. Base future new-grant cost is therefore 10.2% of revenue, downside 12%, upside 9%, with a 9–12% sensitivity. This is economic labor expense, not forecast GAAP amortization. Future grant units are not also added to shares.

The $970.8M unrecognized legacy accounting balance is neither a new cash claim nor an automatic DCF add-back. In the H2 bridge, remove the $283.927M accounting SBC implied by full-year guidance less H1 actual, then charge the chosen post-origin new-grant value. The base charge is $330.616M, making economic EBIT $46.689M lower than v2. This removes legacy accounting recognition within the total accounting-SBC reversal while replacing it with funded future compensation. For later periods, hold v2 pre-SBC margins fixed and substitute the new-grant rate. A separate illustrative accounting reconciliation subtracts and reverses identical legacy recognition; its 1–3-year timing sensitivity has exactly zero value effect. No legacy award value, unrecognized expense deduction or legacy tax windfall is added again.

### Conditional residual claims and asset recovery

The default all-in residual non-operating claim budget is $500M. It is an analyst allowance whose adequacy is assumed, not a verified June liability total, upper bound, or conservative-complete bridge. Its visible references are:
- $167.1M of December 2025 obligations: $70.2M current income taxes plus $96.9M other long-term contractual obligations. The latter included $47.6M uncertain tax and $49.3M primarily pensions/acquisitions. These are historical references, not asserted June balances.
- $195M if the entire closing estimate of EUR150M transaction tax remained unpaid, converted at an assumed 1.30 USD/EUR. This is neither a June unpaid-balance fact nor an exchange-rate observation.
- $55.5M as half of $111M annual note coupons, a reference for interest exposure rather than reported accrued June interest.
- $13.818M June FX derivative liabilities, plus $68.582M unallocated headroom. These references sum to $500M and are all inside that budget.

The budget includes opening non-operating tax, pension deficits, unpaid acquisition/retention claims, accrued financing interest, unmatched deferred-compensation claims and other non-operating contingencies. No listed reference is separately deducted a second time. Gross uncertain-tax benefits of $100.941M and $9.941M associated interest/penalties are not stacked on top of potentially overlapping booked tax claims. The NQDC trust is excluded from asset credit and matched liabilities are excluded from the budget; any unmatched shortfall belongs within it. Any transaction tax already paid receives no second deduction except to the extent the deliberately assumed aggregate budget exceeds actual claims.

Ordinary trade payables, deferred revenue, recurring labor, operating rent and future integration/service costs remain within operating cash flow and NWC. The model does not subtract the entire $823.724M current AP/accrual balance or the $227.835M other long-term accrual balance. Those aggregate disclosures cannot establish how much is non-operating or duplicated elsewhere. Treating all of them as extra debt would risk double-counting operational funding.

The base credits 75% of the $91.392M marketable investments, or $68.544M, for a combined liquidity/tax valuation haircut, and credits no private/equity-method holdings. This haircut is an assumption, not measured tax leakage. Cash credit remains $1.251443B after the $189M operating reserve. The default pool for common and assumed existing awards is EV + $1.251443B + $68.544M − $2.5B debt − $500M residual claims. That pool is allocated across 281.163210M units. There is no further lease, gross UTB, unrecognized SBC, acquisition purchase-price or option-proceeds adjustment.

Claim budgets of $250M/$500M/$800M, unissued RSU assumptions of 3.547462M/4.475463M/6M, and separate option, ESPP, cash-reserve and asset-recovery intervals expose the uncertainty. These are analyst stress intervals, not guaranteed bounds. Every additional $100M net claim reduces default per-share value by about $0.356. Exact June award movements, disaggregated non-operating accruals, unpaid transaction tax, asset availability and post-June movements remain irreducible gaps in the reviewed sources. Unrecorded litigation has no verified finite ceiling. These gaps prevent an unqualified current target, but need not hide explicitly conditional research arithmetic.

## DCF method and independent assumptions

The model uses a six-month H2 2026 stub and ten annual periods, discounted at period end. H1 actual cash flow is already reflected in opening cash and is not valued again. The pre-compensation-normalization FY2026 anchor is GAAP revenue/margin guidance plus $289M acquired-intangible amortization. The H2 accounting-SBC replacement described above then funds economic future grants; R&D and integration costs remain expensed. The source’s dollar reconciliation and margin guidance are inconsistent: $1,799M versus $1,779.75M at the revenue/margin midpoints, a $19.25M or 30.56-basis-point difference. This is larger than normal displayed rounding. The DCF starts from the latter, lower margin-based EBIT plus $289M acquired-intangible amortization, then applies the disclosed future-grant replacement. No blanket non-GAAP margin is treated as owner profit.

Base revenue growth fades from 14% in 2027 to 5% in 2036, with economic margin rising from 32.3% to 33.8% after future grants. Downside growth fades 8% to 2% with 28% mature margin; upside fades 18% to 7% with 37.5% mature margin. These are analyst assumptions, not company targets. R&D and SBC percentage disclosures overlap because R&D includes stock compensation; do not add the two cost categories or subtract them twice.

Growth is funded. The H2 stub charges capex less nonacquisition depreciation, working/operating cash investment and purchased technology. Thereafter positive incremental NOPAT divided by a declining incremental return is reserved as all-in net reinvestment before FCFF. This is a conservative cash-investment budget above expensed R&D, not a claim about a specific capex or acquisition program. It avoids free growth, and includes no acquisition-derived future revenue without consideration.

Discount rates are 12%, 10.5% and 9.25%. The base derives from the [October 16 Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?field_tdr_date_value_month=202610&type=daily_treasury_yield_curve) 10-year yield of 5.09%, [Damodaran](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/home.htm) October implied ERP of 4.20%, and [January software industry](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/Betas.html) cash-adjusted asset beta 1.25. Target debt weighting 5%, 1% debt spread and 24% tax rate are explicit assumptions. The calculated WACC is about 10.25%, rounded up to 10.5%. This is sector-based risk evidence, not a company-specific regression or a current market-cap fit.

Terminal nominal growth is 2%/2.5%/3%, with incremental ROIC 10%/15%/20%. A five-year R&D-capitalized, acquisition-inclusive diagnostic yields approximately 15.3–15.7% in FY2024–2025 using year-end capital and a 24% tax rate; this is an analytical check, not a reported ROIC. R&D is never added back in the actual DCF. Terminal reinvestment is g/ROIC, not zero. Terminal value represents 38.4%, 57.5% and 68.6% of downside/base/upside EV, making the upside particularly sensitive to duration and reinvestment. The package includes a 45-cell WACC/g/ROIC sensitivity.

## Readiness and required review

The ten-year research and v2 corrections passed independent research review. The v3 future-grant normalization, conditional residual budget and award allocation are submitted for new independent review. v3 mechanical tests are internal, not external accounting assurance or approval. The source ledger and SHA-256 checks retain provenance. The public-safe package contains original analysis and selected factual inputs only; no raw filing mirrors, complete third-party transcripts or private retrieval content are redistributed.

Before a current per-share import: replace conditional June assumptions with supported inventory and claim balances or obtain explicit approval for a clearly labeled estimated bridge; verify asset availability and tax leakage; then bridge post-June cash, debt and shares to the intended current date. Do not substitute current shares into a historical cash/debt bridge or move the valuation date without its intervening cash flows.


## Version 2 research corrections
The finite-lived and acquired in-process technology components now reconcile to a consistent total intangible series. Downside terminal ROIC of 10% is below its 12% WACC by two percentage points; terminal growth is value-destructive relative to capital cost. H2 non-acquisition depreciation of $70.740M explicitly repeats H1 as an analyst assumption. Q2 GAAP operating margin of 28.4209% was below the prior 28.5% floor, although both EPS measures exceeded prior upper bounds. The official [February 23 closing release](https://www.cadence.com/en_US/home/company/newsroom/press-releases/pr/2026/cadence-completes-acquisition-of-hexagons-design-and-engineering.html) is now frozen and included in the ledger. The transaction-tax estimate is not evidence of an unpaid June balance. Those v2 corrections left operating EV unchanged and have since passed independent research review. v1/v2 and their review records remain unchanged. v3 changes operating EV only for the explicit future-grant cost normalization; conditional allocation is new, while exact-value/current-date gates remain.

## Version 3 change control
The frozen v2 report and model remain available for comparison. v3 adds compensation-allocation.json, conditional-allocation-sensitivity.json and future-grant-sensitivity.json, updates the executable model and claim assumptions, and retains original source URLs, retrieval dates and file hashes. The source ledger records additional review scope without rewriting originals. No current market quote enters any calculation, and no app edit or publication occurred.
